The frames are then converted to a top-down perspective to measure the distances between individuals in a 2D plane. If any individuals are too close to each other, the system displays a warning by highlighting them with a red frame and a red line.

articleTitle: Design of Plant Leaf Diseases Detection System employing IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Plant diseases can affect an extensive range of commercial crops, and result in a momentous loss in yield. Most diseases are caught by the farmer walking through the field and checking the crop. In this research article, the authors have designed a model for the detection of plant diseases using the Internet of Things (IoT) and Machine Learning (ML) models. Plant diseases constitute a major production hazard in agriculture and major crop failures in the history of man have been due to these diseases. The main goal is to guarantee farmers' early detection of plant diseases, which will reduce the need for pesticides. A more stable and wealthy society is made possible by eliminating the problem of plant diseases. Farmers click the image of the leaf and sensors with Arduino send the real-time data to the cloud where think-speak will visualize the data which was tested and validated using ML models. Support Vector Machine (SVM) and k-NN are used as the ML models implemented by the existing online database. The emergence of accurate techniques in the field of leaf-based image classification has shown impressive results. SVM results in 94.65% accuracy.

articleTitle: Power efficient VLSI architecture based logistic regression for classification of breast cancer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Machine Learning applications involve arithmetic operations, mainly floating-point computations and parameters that are the source of power consumption. This paper proposes a power efficient VLSI architecture, trained and tested on Wisconsin breast cancer (WBC) (original) data set to classify benign or malignant. The precision scaling is carried out on the logistic regression model’s parameters such as weights, bias, and standardized data points, which reduces the complexity of floating-point adder architecture and further the approximate adders are replaced in the mantissa integer adder of floating-point adder architecture, leading to a reduction in area, power, and delay without much compromise in accuracy. Results show an improvement of 93.12% in area, 97.4% in power, and 74% in delay are achieved by half-precision compared to the double-precision. Similarly, there is an improvement of 73.34% in area, 84.63% in power, and 55.65% in delay for single-precision w.r.t double-precision. Further improvement in the area, power, and delay is achieved by replacing the mantissa integer adder with various approximate adders in 16-bit floating-point adder architecture. We proposed five Logistic Regression Models (LRM1 to LRM5), out of which LRM5 is best because it occupies 94.08% less area, consumes 98.21% less power, and 77.68% less delay than the exact double-precision model. Further, results show that LRM5 achieves an improvement of 14.04% in area, 29.66% in power, and 14.12% in delay compared to the half-precision model.

articleTitle: Partial Face Identification using Local Feature Extraction Algorithm on Different Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Face identification is a complex problem with a long history and is currently the subject of much research in unconstrained conditions, including occlusion, facial expression, position change, and lighting. Nevertheless, the occlusion issue receives less attention in current studies. Many sophisticated deep learning and machine learning algorithms have been developed to enhance the identification of occlusion. A new face recognition method: Local Features Extraction with Logistic Classifier, designed to identify someone from the area of their face that is not covered. This proposed work extracts the features by taking the difference of patches and then generating the patch sequence using the k-means clustering algorithm and classifying them using different classifiers. This paper used five classifiers to check their effectiveness in matching the train and test patch sequence. Two public datasets, AR for natural occlusion and ORL for synthetic occlusion are used for experimental work.

articleTitle: BCDNet: GoogLeNet based Bladder Cancer Detection model from Urinary Cytological Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In the realm of medical image processing, computational cytology is a crucial, quickly evolving, yet difficult topic that analyses the digitised cytology images using computer-aided technologies for bladder cancer screening. Both the incidence and mortality of bladder cancer have increased worldwide. This study intends to develop a deep learning based bladder cancer detection model from urinary cytological images for early detection of bladder cancer. The model, called BCDNet: a bladder cancer detection network, inspired form GoogLeNet is trained on voided urine cytological samples of 115 individuals, of which 59 are confirmed cases of Urothelial Cell Carcinoma and the remaining 56 are benign. The input images are first denoised and background removal is applied. These preprocessed cytology images are used to refine the GoogLeNet model in the ratio of 60:20:20, respectively for training, validation and testing. The proposed model is able to achieve and surpass the low sensitivity and low specificity of many of the existing state-of-the-art techniques in detecting the low grade tumors, with a classification accuracy of 95%, sensitivity 81%, and specificity of 91%. It is evident from the experimental results that BCDNet will provide clinicians a non-invasive and economic solution for the early detection of bladder cancer.

articleTitle: A Multilevel Switched Capacitor based High-Gain Non-Isolated Hybrid Switched Inductor Cascaded Boost DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper proposes a Non-Isolated high gain Multilevel Hybrid Switched Inductor Cascaded Boost DC-DC converter (MHSICB). The MHSICB circuit comprises a hybrid switched inductor cell, a multistage switched capacitor cell, and a cascaded boost DC-DC converter, which collectively enhance the overall voltage gain of the converter. The proposed MHSICB demonstrates the capability to achieve an output voltage 14 times higher than the input voltage. The paper provides a comprehensive mathematical analysis for each MODE of operation, elucidating the voltage and current stress experienced by the various components. The MHSICB design incorporates several advantages, including high voltage gain, reduced voltage stress on the active switch, and a relatively lower count of diodes, enabling a higher conversion ratio. A comparative assessment is conducted with other previous topologies reported in the literature. To regulate the output voltage of the MHSICB, a double-loop PI controller is implemented, and its performance is evaluated under sudden disturbances at the load and source sides. The viability and effectiveness of the MHSICB are validated through MATLAB simulation results.

articleTitle: Additional logic for Alpha Plane Algorithm under Ground faults
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Transmission lines are protected by the phase-based Alpha Plane Relaying method. Because of the large Restraining Region (RR), there is strong security against synchronization errors, channel delay, CT saturation, and line charging current. However, under outfeed situations, when connected to a ground with high resistance, the APR becomes less sensitive. (HRF) faults. Decreasing dependability in the presence of three-phase faults with low resistance and close-in faults. Thus, the sequence-based APR offers increased sensitivity at the expense of computational complexity and burden. As a result, this study uses the concept of the average value (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Avg</inf>) of both end instantaneous currents. In which, high resistance internal faults are confirmed using the polarity of I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Avg</inf> as an add-on logic to the traditional APR. By doing this, Negative and zero can be used to avoid the need for sequence components. The proposed auxiliary logic for the 9-bus, 110 kV is examined, 50 Hz WSCC (Western System Coordinating Council) System in order to validate it. The simulated outcomes under different failure scenarios discovered authenticated outcomes.

Author Keywords: fault resistance and Current transformer core saturation

articleTitle: Energy Efficient Approximate Floating Point Divider
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This work proposes a novel approach to designing an approximate floating point divider with an error percentage lesser than one percent. The proposed design is derived from the mantissa division analysis. Subtracting the lower 16-bits of the mantissa rather than dividing it and the rest of the most significant 8-bits are divided using standard division hardware will guarantee less than 1% error in output compared to the existing dividers from the literature. The proposed design saves energy 99.61% and 32.18% than the conventional floating point divider and approximate FPAD, respectively. The proposed design does not use any look-up mechanism and error correction circuits.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning and IoT-based Anti-spoofing Technique for Liveness Detection and Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Security systems used in public and corporate sectors these days are becoming more and more biometrics dependent. Face recognition is one of the most prominent tools used in authentication systems. It used to involve creating a digital template of the face of a person and identifying it, which is a unique physical characteristic for each and every person. But this method of biometrics is susceptible to certain threats. The system can be fooled using the image of the person or by displaying videos or photos of the person in front of the camera. To overcome this problem, certain methods have been proposed, which include texture analysis, frequency analysis, 3D face shaping, etc. The constraint of these methods is that they require high computational powers because of the length and complexity of the codes. These methods are suitable to be implemented on high-end devices, such as smartphones, laptops, etc. The aim of this paper is to provide a method for liveness detection suitable for edge devices. A method that is much more reliable and uses less computational power is proposed. Raspberry pi is used to implement the proposed technique which itself is an edge device. The two major complications of a facial recognition system are tackled separately by using the algorithms of eye blink detection and object detection.

articleTitle: Fault Detection and Localization in Distribution System using Sparse Matrix Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The increasing emphasis on reducing carbon emissions and addressing climate change has led to a growing role for renewable energy sources. The integration of distributed generators and electric vehicles into the distribution networks has made fault diagnosis more complex due to the impact on network operations. To modernize these grids, advanced telecommunications technology and high-frequency sensors are being deployed. Consequently, an effective fault diagnosis strategy is critical to effectively utilize the grid’s equipment and minimize the impact of faults on the system and its components. Quick detection and localization of faults lead to faster isolation and restoration of supply thereby improving power quality and network reliability. This paper presents a sparse matrix reconstruction technique to detect faults with the help of PMU. In this paper, optimal placement of PMUs is done first, and then positive seq voltage of both pre-fault and during-fault conditions are measured. The difference between them is then used to recover the current change vector through the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) with the help of which fault is detected. The proposed algorithm is tested on a modified IEEE 9 bus test case system modeled on PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Modelling and Implementation of 0.5 V to 1.8 V Level Shifter Reflected output and Dual Wilson Current Mirror Technique
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The Voltage Level Shifter is used for changing the signal's voltage domain. A voltage range with a single voltage domain, differ from a voltage range in another voltage domain. When a chip operates in various voltage domains, this is necessary. In an electrical circuit, a logic-level shifter changes the voltage or logic level. Compatibility between ICs with different voltage needs, such as CMOS and TTL, is created thanks to logic shifters. In order to reduce power dissipation, two times the supplied voltage approach is widely used in today’s VLSI architecture. To convert small voltages to large voltages, level shifters come in handy. Using a level shifter, the Wilson current mirror was demonstrated with low power, high-efficiency in changing levels. Cadence Virtuoso and 180nm technologies were used to implement the recommended design. It changes input signal ranges between 50 mV and around 1 V at result with a single WCMLS. The proposed design could be implemented in Cadence Virtuoso and 45nm technologies, using Dual Wilson Current Mirror resulting in changing input signal as down as 0.5 V to around 1.8 V as result, decreasing latency and power consumption with high-efficiency.

Author Keywords: Wilson Current Mirror based Level Shifter (WCMLS)

articleTitle: Optimization Techniques for Car Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The optimization is a key concept in machine learning, it can be used to find the best parameters for a machine learning algorithm, or to find the best way to solve a problem. Price determination for a secondhand car is typically a laborious and error-prone process if done manually. However, this method would be made simpler and more adaptable by applying machine learning techniques to the issue. This can be viewed as a prediction task using machine learning, where the model will be trained on previously collected data while also emphasizing the factors that impact price most. This study compares the effectiveness of various machine-learning algorithms and optimization techniques, and it suggests a novel machine-learning strategy paired with optimization algorithms for car price prediction. This kind of regression problem can be solved using a variety of machine-learning methods. These techniques can be used in conjunction with optimization algorithms to raise the model's overall prediction efficiency and accuracy. In this work, we tried seven optimization algorithms for model building and find the effectiveness of those algorithms. Finally using the Genetic algorithm and Random forest we achieved an R2 score of 0.91, a Mean absolute error of 01.49, a Mean squared error of 10.27, and a Root mean squared error of 03.20.

articleTitle: A Frequency Agile Textile Based Wearable Antenna for On Body Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Here we present, a frequency tunable textile based wearable monopole antenna with center frequency at 2.45 GHz and at 5.2 GHz for wearable and biomedical telemetry application. Switching mechanism of two PIN diodes have been utilized to achieve the frequency agility. This antenna exhibits 17.14% impedance bandwidth at 2.45 GHz and 10% impedance bandwidth at 5.2 GHz when simulated in two-layer phantom model. Our proposed antenna satisfies the specified limit of specific absorption rate (SAR) as set by the FCC (Federal Communication Commission).

articleTitle: Optimal Unit Scheduling using Modified Ant Lion Optimization Algorithm for Secure Operation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This article presents the solution for the OPF problem using Modified Ant Lion Optimization (MALO) based on a chaotic map to enhance its initial random walk, leading to better solutions. The MALO algorithm minimizes cost by computing the generators' real output power and finding the best OPF solution. This analysis uses a standard 24-hour data of IEEE 14 bus test system for OPF solution. Further, the results obtained from the proposed MALO algorithm have been compared with particle swarm optimization and teaching learning-based optimization algorithm. Results show that the proposed MALO algorithm is flexible, more accurate, and applicable for the standard IEEE 14 bus test system.

articleTitle: Dual-stream Mobile Beacon Based Localization Scheme for Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Knowing each sensor location is essential for efficiently managing the wireless sensor network. There are many localization schemes; some presume to use the mobile beacon because it has much potential. This paper presents a novel mobile beacon-based range-based localization scheme. In the proposed method, a mobile beacon traverses the area with two onboard Zigbee and a magnetometer. These radio transceivers are kept diagonal from each other, where the diagonal distance is symmetric to a square geometry. The mobile beacon broadcasts two beacon messages at each beacon point. The sensor node receives the beacon messages containing the beacon point coordinates of each Zigbee and the direction of the mobile beacon from the magnetic compass. The sensor node utilizes the beacon information and identifies its initial proximity using the received signal strength (RSS) and the direction of the mobile beacon. The sensor node estimates its distance from the mobile beacon using RSS and utilizes the geometric formulation to locate its position. The geometric formulation estimates two positions of the sensor node. To identify the valid position of the sensor node, the sensor node utilizes the beacon information. The simulation and experimental results show that the proposed scheme localizes the sensor node with minimum localization error.

articleTitle: Antenna Substrate Requirements For Integration Over Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper presents the requirement of antenna substrate for some specific application—likewise the need for a patch antenna for the integration over a solar panel. The antenna is made for a resonant frequency range of 2.2 to 2.4 GHz. The antenna’s performance is compared by using PET (polyethylene terephthalate), PDMS (polydimethylsiloxane), Plexiglass, and fr4 epoxy as substrates. In further studies, the antenna is mounted over a solar panel. Through which the observations are made on the basis of the comparison of the better performance of the antenna.

articleTitle: Armchair Graphene Nanoribbon Resonant Tunneling Diode: Influence of numbers of V-cuts as barrier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The arm-chair nanoribbon (AGNR) band gap can be modulated by introducing a geometrical V-cut on the edge. By introducing such cuts in a certain region of pristine AGNR, heterojunction can be created. This heterojunction can be further utilized to create a double barrier quantum well (DBQW) to form a quantized quasi-energy state between barriers. In this paper, we propose a method to construct a resonant tunneling diode by imposing V-cuts as barriers in pristine AGNR, and the effect of the number of cuts in the barrier region is investigated. For numerical calculation, we use the nearest neighbor tight-binding method along with non-equilibrium green function (NEGF) formalism to study transport properties.

articleTitle: Hybrid of DNN Feature Extraction and Ensemble Classification for Identification of Esophagitis and Barretts in Upper Gastrointestinal Tract Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The main focus of this work is to perform a computer vision classification method for upper gastrointestinal tract image analysis with a pre-trained deep learning features extraction stage. An open-source dataset was used containing images of upper gastrointestinal tract problems including Esophagitis (260 images) and Barretts (94 images). In the given input, image pre-processing with image re-sizing, and noise removal was applied, and then finally working extraction of features using pre-trained deep neural networks. The extracted data from the second last layer of pre-trained models represents the most prominent features. The extracted features are then classified with the help of machines and ensemble learning methods. The improved classification results have been identified using pre-trained models based on feature extraction techniques in comparison to traditional deep learning models.

articleTitle: Design of MIMO-FSO based IoT system
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Free space optics (FSO) allows extensive transfer rate, low energy consumption and wide spectrum along with immunity against electromagnetic interference. This work reports a 10×10 Gbps multiple input multiple output FSO (MIMO-FSO) based internet of things (IoT) system under the impact of diverse climate conditions has been reported. The novelty of this work is to design an IoT based high speed as well as long reach wireless transmission system considering various environmental crises. The results show that FSO transmission range of 130 km for clear weather conditions. Also, the system using optimum value of transmission as well as reception aperture diameters means 10 and 40 cm respectively, FSO range can be considerably extended more than 110 km.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Processing with Normalized AttUNet
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The goal is enhancement of images with different water types and to achieve visual quality improvement of the underwater images. Poor visibility in underwater images is a result of color casts, low contrast, and particle dispersion, all of which are caused by wavelength-dependent and distance-dependent attenuation. To address these degradation issues and to learn water type desensitized features, normalization is applied along both spatial and channel dimensions. In the spatial dimension, instance whitening is applied, to decorrelate activations. Moreover, channel-wise normalization is used to manipulate the first two moments of the channel activations. Then, attention is used to provide weights to certain features based on their importance. We proposed a lightweight model named Normalised AttUNet to provide fast processing time for diverse water type images, while still maintaining comparable PSNR.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Adhesion Force (Fadh) for Microelectromechanical (MEM)-based Non-Volatile Memory (NVM) Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Microelectromechanical (MEM) non-volatile memory (NVM) uses an adhesion-based approach to gain non-volatility. In such memory design not only is the opening and closing of the device mechanism is import but adhesion is also a main concern. Adhesion between the two contacting surfaces implies volatile or non-volatile behaviour. Most of the devices are failed during their operation after fabrication. Thus, we have presented a simulation study on the adhesion force between two surfaces. This study gives the exact data for adhesion failed less device. Simulation is for the two structural materials (gold and molybdenum) most widely used in the MEM. Also, successfully fabricated and characterise the NVM cell based on the simulation.

articleTitle: Simulating Quantum Hardware using Qiskit Metal
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The process of building a quantum circuit often consists of several steps. We need a quantum framework that enables us to create these circuits and a simulation environment that enables us to analyse the circuit in order to execute these circuits. Qiskit Metal, an open-source framework made available by IBM, is the name of the quantum framework we used. Ansys Electronic Desktop is the modelling software used to evaluate these built-in circuits. In this paper, we go over how to build a quantum circuit and its simulation on Ansys’ electronic desktop. The conventional methods of modelling the circuit—manually by launching the project in Ansys or automatically through a code—don’t always work. This paper will examine the alternative ways of allowing simulations on quantum hardware projects.

articleTitle: Automating Citation Intent Classification on SciCite Dataset
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Scientific papers often contain citations that provide important information on the background, methods used, and results obtained. Identifying the intent of these citations is a critical machine learning problem, and it is also essential for the automated analysis of scientific literature. The SciCite dataset, consisting of 11,020 rows and 15 features, was used for this purpose. Preprocessed data was then fed to machine learning models such as KNN, Random Forest Classifier, Light Gradient Boost Classifier, Gradient Boost Classifier, and XGBoost. A comparison was drawn among these models to identify the one that yields the highest weighted F1 score, which was found to be 87% for the Light Gradient Boost Classifier. The findings of this work demonstrate the effectiveness of using Machine Learning models and word embedding techniques, such as Doc2Vec and GloVe, to accurately classify the intent of citations in scientific papers.

articleTitle: QLEN: A Load Distribution Algorithm to Improve QoS Factors Among Fog Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This article entails the proposition of a heuristic multi-objective algorithm for load distribution among fog devices. The decision for routing is made based on a weighted heuristic. The proposed algorithm, QLEN aims to improve three quality of service factors, namely L (load balancing efficiency), E (energy consumption) and N (network usage); hence the name QLEN. The importance of these parameters can be varied according to the application. This is done by adjusting the weights to suit the needs of the incoming tasks. For the default use case, the weights are tuned for the optimization of all three of the parameters. These optimal weights are calculated using stochastic gradient descent. QLEN is compared against fundamental load balancing algorithms such as Round Robin, Throttled Round Robin and Priority Based Load Balancing algorithm. The environment simulates a health monitoring application, using the iFogSim simulator. The results show that QLEN consistently outperforms the compared algorithms with respect to the targeted parameters. The efficiency of load distribution achieved by QLEN on average performs 1.69% better than all the three algorithms; at the same time showing 54.86% lesser network usage, 3413.33 MJ lesser energy consumption and 10.39% reduced redirection to the cloud. The algorithm also scales efficiently, showing better performance as the number of fog devices increases.

articleTitle: A PUF Based Authentication Schemes for UAV
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In recent years Unmanned Aerial vehicles (UAVs) have grown in popularity due to their adaptability and wide variety of uses, which include aerial photography, videography, surveying, mapping, wildlife monitoring, search and rescue, and military surveillance. But, because of growing concern over authentication and security, which are critical in UAVs to prevent unauthorized access, secure sensitive data, prevent malicious attacks, and comply with laws, we want a more sophisticated and computationally effective security architecture. Hence, this paper investigates the authenticity of communication between a UAV and a ground base station (GS). It proposes a novel authentication technique that uses the Challenge Response Pair (CRP) and Physically Unclonable Function (PUF) to produce a unique key for each communication session. We used the Automatic Validation of Internet Security Protocols and Applications (AVISPA) program to assess the suggested authentication technique and found that it prevents unauthorized access and alteration of data exchanged between the UAV and GS. The suggested technique is lightweight and does not require a large number of processing resources, making it ideal for usage in resource-constrained UAVs.

articleTitle: DC Nano-Grid with Power Management System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The DC residential nano-grid is typically a combination of renewable energy sources (RES) like solar panels, fuel-cells, micro wind together with batteries (EES), and DC loads for isolated buildings. For solar and fuel cell DC-DC Boost converter is used, bi-directional converter is used for ESS however buck/boost converter are required for loads. The maximum benefit of multi-source can only be achieved by optimal load and source scheduling whereas priority load and non-priority load needs to be distinguished and controlled using appropriate power management algorithm. In this paper, a new algorithm is developed for the central controller to manage the power flows between the RES, ESS and priority and non-priority loads. The real-time data is sent to the central controller to operate DC nano-grid in different modes based on power generation and load information. The proposed central controller and power management system is implemented and validated using the MATLAB Simulink platform that it effectively maintains the DC bus voltage at 48 V, adjust the voltage and power of every unit and balance what energy flows in the system irrespective of variations in switching functioning ways, radiation and climate, and loads.

articleTitle: Resistorless Wave Filter Design employing DXCCDITA
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper illustrates an active filter design using modern current mode building block termed as Dual X Current-Conveyor Differential Input Trans-Conductance Amplifier (DXCCDITA) and few MOS transistors. In this proposed wave filter technique, only MOS transistors are used for the realization of active block DXCCDITA and passive components. An elementary series inductor is realized using three MOS based resistor, a grounded Capacitor and two DXCCDITA. The proposed wave filter is designed for fifth and sixth order low pass filter and well verified through PSPICE simulation using 0.18 µm CMOS technology parameter.

Author Keywords: Dual X Current-Conveyor Differential Input Trans-conductance Amplifier (DXCCDITA)

articleTitle: A Secured Audio Encryption Algorithm Based On Gauss and Henon Chaotic Maps
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The complex and erratic dynamics of chaotic maps can be used for secure communication because they generate a key stream of data that appears random and difficult to predict. This paper proposes a new audio encryption algorithm based on 1D Gauss and 2D Henon chaotic maps. We employed two chaotic maps of various dimensions since a single chaotic map has a smaller key space and less security. The two chaotic maps are used to produce keys and these keys would be employed to carry out the operation of permutation and logical XOR operation upon the samples of the given input audio signal. The key generated by a 1D Gauss map is used to carry out the permutation operation. Moreover, the key generated by a 2D Henon chaotic map is used to carry out the logical operation. Several audio security tests and statistical analyses show that the suggested algorithm has good attack and security performance. The performance results of the offered algorithm reveal that it can be competitive with certain other previously proposed audio encryption techniques.

articleTitle: Fault Detection Algorithm Based on Resistance Approach for DC Micro-grids
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Due to the advancement of power electronic converters as well as the absence of a zero crossing point, conventional protection techniques are limited to DC microgrids. In addition, traditional methods may fail to operate during low-magnitude fault currents. In the proposed protection method, the intelligent electronic devices (IEDs) situated on either end of the line attain the locally sensed values of voltage and current samples and determines the apparent resistance. Subsequently, the fault detection condition is derived with the aid of threshold value of resistance and estimated resistance. In this detection process, pre-fault voltages and currents are used to estimate the value of threshold resistance. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed technique, numerous fault cases such as different fault resistances, multiple fault locations in a line, different system configurations and idle operation of renewable energy sources were simulated in the MATLAB/Simulink software on 350 V and 500 kW rated ring configured DC microgrid. It confirms that the proposed technique effectively detects the faults under various unhealthy as mentioned above.

Author Keywords: power electronic converter and threshold resistance

articleTitle: Temporal Dynamics of Likes and Retweets Engagement of Indian Politicians on Twitter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: A multitude of population utilises social media in today’s era. Social Media provides an efficient platform for the exchange of information and rapid propagation of ideas. Politicians, celebrities, content authors, as well as businesses in the health, real estate, beauty, and fashion industries, among others, greatly benefit from this platform. Hence, its study is of paramount significance and the principal actors of social media are - influencers. Our work is built upon the study of influencers of politics in our country - our very own Indian Politicians. Six Indian politicians have been chosen and their Twitter activity has been monitored around the time when Delhi Municipal Corporation elections (December, 2022) were approaching. On investigation, some crucial facts were found regarding the life of a tweet, the importance of mentions and media content in a tweet and much more. These key findings have been explained in this paper which can help influencers achieve better engagement on their tweets. Along with this, some machine learning models have been trained to predict the engagement on a given tweet and achieved the highest accuracy of 80.1%. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first attempt of conducting such thorough study on the temporal dynamics of engagement for Indian Politicians.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wave Function Collapse Algorithm using Bitwise Operations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The wave function collapse algorithm is a method for generating procedural content in the field of computer graphics and video games introduced in 2016. In this algorithm, a large number of potential outcomes are represented as a wave function, and as the algorithm progresses, the wave function collapses into a single, definite state that represents the final output. Over the years there have been advances in improving design constraints, automatic rule writing and applying Wave Function Collapse in other domains like navigation etc. This paper aims to improve the runtime and size of the Wave Function Collapse algorithm by modifying its implementation using a Bitwise Grid and bitwise operations. A terrain is generated using 4 states. The constraints or rules are defined using a new constraint matrix according to which many random terrains are generated quickly. After various tests and iterations, we can conclude that Bitwise Grid implementation can produce 8000 terrains in approximately 1 second whereas the original implementation took 8 seconds.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Symmetrical And Asymmetrical Submodule Topologies of Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Nowadays, modular multilevel converters (MMCs) are gaining extreme attention to fulfill the electrical power demand of industry 4.0. In this regard, novel MMC submodule (SM) topologies are being explored as well as proposed with reduced component counts to attain higher levels of output voltage. This paper presents a comparative analysis of symmetrical and asymmetrical submodule topologies with a view to the generation of higher output voltage levels and lesser component requirements. Classical SM topologies like half-bridge submodules (HB-SM) and mixed cell submodules having symmetrical and asymmetrical capacitor voltage based three phase MMCs using two SMs/arm are simulated here with the help of MATLAB/Simulink environment to validate their performance. A quantitative and qualitative comparison between symmetrical and asymmetrical submodule topologies is also presented in terms of the component requirements, output current/voltage total harmonic distortion (THD), capacitor ripple voltages, control complexity, fault handling capability, etc. Asymmetrical SMs have the advantage of reduced and robust circuitry while symmetrical SMs have the advantage of lesser voltage stress and equal ratings of control switches.

articleTitle: Super-twisting sliding mode control of a new muti-scroll hidden chaotic system
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This report uses a control technique on the basis of a super-twisting sliding mode algorithm to stabilize the response of a new multi-scroll hidden chaotic system. The new hidden chaotic system is generated from an existing system. The system properties, i.e., Lyapunov exponents, Lyapunov dimension, dissipativity, etc., are analyzed. Compared to the existing mother chaotic system, the generated system is more chaotic and more complex. The new system also has multi-stability property. Subsequently, a second-order sliding surface and super-twisting control law are designed to achieve chattering-free sliding motion to control the newly developed system. With only one control signal(in a 3D system), the chaotic system is successfully controlled. The convergence of the chaotic states to the origin is proved mathematically as well verified from the simulation results. Moreover, the robustness of the controlled system is successfully validated in the presence of matched disturbance and parameter uncertainty.

articleTitle: A Review on Role of Epitaxial Engineering in Improving the Drive Current and Subthreshold Swing in Area Scaled Tunnel FETs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In this work, to support the need of ultra-low power applications with "Always-ON" feature, a review of area-scaled tunneling is carried out in different Field Effect Transistor (FET) architectures. Area-scaled tunnel FETs (TFETs) provides the solution to low drive current and degraded Subthreshold Swing (SS) in tunnel FETs by significantly increasing the area of cross-section available for Band-to-Band Tunneling (BTBT) by depositing an epitaxial layer above the source region. We have investigated the role of epitaxial engineering in ultra scaled architectures like FinFET and Gate-All-Around (GAA) FET. Gate over source overlap length (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GS,ov</inf>), epitaxial-layer thickness (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EPI</inf>) and epitaxial-layer doping (N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">EPI</inf>) are considered as the key parameters of epitaxial based TFETs. It has been investigated that the performance parameters like ON-current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>), OFF-current (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf>), I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">on</inf>/I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">off</inf> and SS are significantly affected by employing the epi-layer. Optimum value of these key parameters should be carefully chosen to outperform when compared with their counterparts.

articleTitle: Analytical Voltage Sag and Swell Characterization Using Differential Geometry
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This paper presents a unique method for analysing voltage dips and swells using differential geometrical algebra. Differential geometry has been applied to interpret synthetic electrical signals as curves. This is possible since the instantaneous amplitude of a sinusoidal wave can be defined as a curve. This strategy is based on the rotating Frenet-Serret (TNB) frame, defined at each point along the curve. It serves as the basis for the method. Because the Frenet Frame is only locally specified for a curve if the derivative components are present, the moving frame velocity represents the changes in the events in the system. This method provides a better comprehension of circumstances such as sag and swells in contrast to prior methods that utilised the Clark and Park transformation to extract the event information and represent it using ellipsoidal geometry.

articleTitle: Optimal Model Parameter Identification of Solid Oxide Fuel Cell Using Honey Badger Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: This article presents a model parameter identification approach for solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) based on honey badger algorithm. Mathematical model of SOFC is observed as a complex and multivariate optimization problem. Metaheuristic optimization algorithms are seen as competent to solve multivariate and complex problems effectively and efficiently. To identify unknown model parameters accurately, an objective function based on error minimization is used in this article. The error function is described as the sum of squared error (SSE) between the evaluated and experimental voltage. It is proven that honey badger algorithm calculates the model parameter effectively with the value of SSE as 1.51E-05, 1.52E-05 and 1.04E-05 at three different temperatures, viz. 800°C, 900°C and 940°C. Also, the efficiency of the honey badger algorithm for parameter identification approach is compared with other competitive algorithms such as bald eagle search (BES), flower pollination (FPA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and grey wolf optimization (GWO). An adequate closeness between the estimated and experimental values confirms the algorithm’s accuracy. Furthermore, statistical study, including statistical indices like mean, standard deviation, minimum and maximum values, proves its superiority over other competitive algorithms. Also, a box plot study has been done to check the algorithm’s robustness. Small interquartile range and median value proves that the honey badger algorithm outperforms other algorithms used and thus estimates the model parameters effectively.

articleTitle: Detection of Canine Parvovirus using ELM and Support Vector Machine Algorithm from Blood Tests
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Canine parvovirus is a widespread disease affecting dogs, particularly young puppies. Most frequently, a fecal ELISA test is used to detect this virus. This test does not guarantee the presence of the virus in the dog and costs between 3500 and 4000 RS (INR). Generally, Veterinary doctors conduct blood tests of the affected dogs and then recommend the fecal ELISA test since different parameters of blood tests also cannot accurately predict the presence of Parvovirus. In this paper, a novel method of Parvovirus detection is proposed based on the blood chemistry report of the dog. This method uses a Semi-supervised Support Vector Machine (SSVM) based model to detect the virus using the blood chemistry parameters of the animal with labeled and unlabeled data.

articleTitle: Router-Router Switching Communication and Logic Verification with Configured Hardware Chip
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The primary function of a router is to simultaneously connect many networks. It operates on the network layer as well. The main purpose of a switch is to provide a connection between many devices at once. It uses the data link layer to operate. The research article proposes chip communication between two networks in which two different clusters of 8 routers are communicating. The chip design is carried out using Xilinx ISE 14.7 software and behavior simulation and logic testing is carried out in Modelsim 10.0 software in which 64-bit data communication is verified in router-router communication. The design approach is a significant effort for effective network-on-chip (NoC) Communication. The novelty of the design is that the chip configuration is scalable and can be extended to a larger extent based on system requirements.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Non-Linear Kalman Filters for Li-ion Battery SoC Estimation with RLS-VDF Technique for Parameters Identification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Accurate state of charge (SoC) estimation is necessary for safe and efficient functioning of lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries in a miscellany of applications, such as portable gadgets, grid storage systems, and electric cars. However, the accuracy of SoC estimation highly depend on the accuracy of the battery model and its parameters identification, which is often difficult to obtain due to the complicated behavior of Li-ion batteries. Recursive Least Square variable directional forgetting (RLS-VDF) technique is a parameter identification algorithm that can improve the parameters estimation of the battery model in real-time, leading to more accurate battery models for non-linear Kalman filters (NLKFs). NLKFs have been generally employed for SoC estimation due to their capability to handle non-linearities and uncertainties in the battery system. This paper assessed the effectiveness of various NLKFs, such as extended Kalman filter, adaptive extended Kalman filter (AEKF), unscented Kalman filter (UKF), and adaptive improved unscented Kalman filter (AIUKF) with the RLS-VDF technique for parameter identification. The accuracy and robustness of the various NLKFs are evaluated using experimental data from a commercial Li-ion battery. The results indicate that the AIUKF with RLS-VDF provides the most accurate and robust SoC estimation performance among the four filters.

Author Keywords: recursive least square variable direction forgetting

articleTitle: Are we undermining data breaches? Protecting education sector from data breaches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Compliance with data protection frameworks such as GDPR is a new necessity for a data fiduciary. Indian DPDPB-2022 (draft) is also one step towards this. Applying appropriate security and safeguard to data is an essential requisite in the framework and the absence of it may lead to a data breach. Currently, data breaches are happening and education sectors are being actively targeted along with other sectors. On regular basis, multiple incidents are announced under this category. This is possible due to more information being available to threat actors easily due to poor security infrastructures. The institutions are not able to determine the scope, consequences, and impact of data breaches and are not able to take corrective actions to revamp the security.In this paper, we have analyzed the latest data breaches as claimed by threat actors over public breach forums such as breached. We discuss common causes that may lead to breaches, challenges in their prevention, and issues in data breach handling (if an event happens). We analyzed the reasons why data breaches are indeed threatful to an educational institution and should not be undermined. Redesigning systems and infrastructure after considering data breach consequences is a new essential requisite to provide greater security assurance. We provide a detailed list of constituents that needs to be integrated to prevent data breaches. The descriptions show the necessity and efficacy of the constituents. Each method is equally important and provides a stronger level of compliance to prevent data breaches and minimize the impact of a data breach (if happens) to the organization.

articleTitle: An Early Recommendation Tool to Enhance Medicinal Plant Growth based on GIS and Soil Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Ayurvedic medicinal plants are in the spotlight, solving the major problem which is being arisen in the modern world. Ayurvedic plants are acquiring great attention in the prescription field owing to having fewer deadly effects on human life and being much less expensive than chemical-based medicines. Based on the available statistics many scientists have shown plenty of interest in the research of recognizing and nurturing medicinal plants. The serious concern is the extension of medicinal plants affecting the life of the needy. In this paper, a novel method is proposed to identify the geographical location and the best suitable soil type of the medicinal plant species in the region of Karnataka, India. The work targets on few vulnerable plants and employs the random forest algorithm (decision tree algorithm) for the recommendation of the medicinal plants based on the soil and GIS data. Hence, an appropriate and easy access solution for the real-time information on the Ayurvedic herbs of Karnataka. The expected outcome of the system is a recommendation tool to grow, conserve and enhance the knowledge of medicinal plants by using the decision tree algorithm, revealing the vital details of herbs such as conservation status, soil type, region name, geo-location and climate condition for the growth of the medicinal plants to help its stakeholders. The system helps to preserve the ancient and traditional medicinal knowledge by identifying the medicinal plants using decision tree based predictive model.

articleTitle: Thyristor dodged VSC: An Enhanced Efficiency Conception for HVDC Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The ever-increasing energy demand requires efficient transmission of power from the point of generation to the point of utilization. Several converters are used in the modern-day HVDC transmission path; one such converter is a modular multilevel converter (MMC). It offers several advantages, the primary being reduced switching losses. But it uses fully controlled devices like IGBT, increasing the conduction loss. Various MMC-derived topologies have been published since the idea of MMC emerged to reduce conduction losses, yet none could achieve the efficiency of a line-commutated converter. Integration of thyristors in voltage source converter (VSC) to produce a hybrid topology offering better performance is the idea of this article. Including a thyristor provides superior characteristics such as higher voltage blocking capability, reliability, high surge current rating, efficient power handling capability and low on-state losses. The article presents the emergence, assessment and topology preference of hybrid converters incorporating IGBTs and thyristors. A comparative study of all the recent topologies is carried out to identify their advantages and limitations.

articleTitle: Enhancement in IoT through Custom Instruction Set Architectures and TinyML: Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The Internet of Things or IoT means to the confluence of the network of interconnected devices, the technologies that enable communication among these devices, and between these devices and the cloud. IoT contains embedded CPUs for performing a variety of functions. The processors for enhancing IoT applications form an active area of research in the domain of Computer Architecture. Embedded processors are resource and power-constrained challenging the execution of deep learning and machine learning algorithms. One proposed solution in literature is TinyML (Tiny Machine Learning) to overcome this limitation. TinyML architecture for IoT aims to deliver low latency, and effective bandwidth usage, reinforce data security, enhance privacy, and save costs. TinyML enables IoT devices to perform ML computations to be performed in the edge and avoid frequent access to the cloud which increases the performance. This paper presents a review of processor designs that are designed for TinyML architecture. For addressing other important issues in IoT a review of custom ISAs (Instruction Set Architectures) developed is also presented in this review.

articleTitle: Security Attacks and it’s Countermeasures on Smart Grid: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The recent advent of Smart Grid has influenced the creation of Big Data in the field of energy consumption and also have influenced the security concerns with the User data. Smart Grid facilitates an efficient and reliable end to end two-way delivery system. The electricity consumption for an individual user is available at real time. It also, enables real-time monitoring and controlling of power system from utilities perspective, which helps them reducing the power losses. So, it is going to replace the old methodologies of sharing electricity, to fulfill the exponential needs of electricity in terms of flexibility, reliability and quality, etc. Therefore the inheriting this advanced power system of electricity grid, alongside communication and networking mechanism in smart grid is taken up in order to exponentially increase the existing of network of smart grid in upcoming time. The success of smart grid mainly depends on its communication. The architect and developer has to make sure that every single smallest entity is in connection with every other part in the smart grid in order to maintain a successful architecture. But in modern era whenever we talk and work on any sort of data, it comes up with its own challenges to secure the data and maintain the Integrity, Confidentiality and Availability. Using this sort of communication which makes one reliable on the technology data from the distress regarding security and further the aspects of privacy also jumps into the scenario. The aim of the study is to find out the different sort of possible attacks on Smart Grid and it’s solution.

articleTitle: A Novel Attribute based Encryption with implicit user authentication for Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Cloud computing is gaining popularity steadily. It has evolved into a method for data storage and retrieval from any location at any time. It is one of the most popular settings for the maintenance and administration of data, information, and services internationally in this era of globalisation. Before stating that cloud computing is the way of the future, however, there are a few security concerns that must be resolved. The challenges include unauthorised access, confidentiality, and data privacy. Out of numerous suggested security systems, attribute-based encryption (ABE) might be considered one of the most viable security and privacy-preserving solutions in cloud settings. The majority of ABE approaches now in practice rely on expensive bilinear maps and pairing operations. In this paper, a novel ABE for cloud environments is suggested that makes use of elliptic curve cryptography. The main operation of the suggested method is simple scalar point multiplication over an elliptic curve, and uses bottom up approach across the access tree to provide implicit authentication of the user. The intractability of the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP) serves as the foundation for the suggested technique’s security assumption.

articleTitle: A Wideband Single Polarization Radio Receiver - Precursor to Low Frequency Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The low frequency radio telescope (LFRT) is a new initiative undertaken by the Raman Research Institute (RRI) for exploring the radio sky at low frequencies. Transient sky till date, has remained almost unexplored and is expected to open up a new dimension of astronomical exploration. For detecting transients routinely over a large volume of space at frequencies below 300 MHz, there does not seem to exist anywhere in the world an optimized setup with required sensitivity. In this context, a wide band single polarization radio receiver as a precursor to the LFRT has been built by RRI to operate in the frequency range of 30 – 360 MHz. This has been realized using two 1:3 bandwidth antennas covering the frequency ranges 30 – 90 MHz and 120 – 360 MHz respectively. It is expected to have i) instantaneous bandwidth of about 300 MHz and ii) a wide field coverage of 2π Steradian. We describe in this paper, the design of a wide band radio receiver system consisting of i) frequency independent broadband antennas ii) compact analog delay line for producing multiple beams in the sky iii) a high dynamic range front end receiver and iv) a 1024 channel precision spectrometer, along with its performance characteristics. The initial results obtained confirm i) the frequency independent behaviour of the antenna over its design bandwidth and the ii) the delay expected out of the compact analog line implemented on the water-based substrate.

articleTitle: Exploring Stock Price Prediction Techniques: A Systematic Review and Empirical Study of Pattern Recognition and Hybrid Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Stock prices typically fluctuate in the short and long term in response to trading and financial activity that reflects various forms of recurrent patterns. These patterns are governed by several unknown aspects in the market, such as firm performance evaluation, government policies, and different government-related or other forms of news. Time series, on the other hand, are non-stationary and very variable. As a result, stock price prediction is one of the most difficult undertakings in the stock market. Researchers have used a variety of pattern recognition techniques, as well as hybridization with other significant techniques, to solve the prediction difficulty. In this work, various stock prediction techniques (Specifically pattern recognition techniques) were reviewed systematically. To validate the pattern recognition technique a well-defined case of bull flag pattern recognition technique accompanied by the technical feature of stop loss and book profit has been studied and analyzed in this work. An empirical study, in this case, shows that intraday returns and average returns are higher with the bull flag template matching technique. In this paper, a brief taxonomy of the various prediction techniques has been done. A detailed discussion of different pattern recognition techniques has been done separately. To understand the hybrid pattern recognition technique in the stock market a case is studied where the pattern technique is combined with technical analysis and corresponding performance in various stock markets has been studied. The result shows that the hybrid technique gives returns much above the average investor made it in the market.

articleTitle: Edge computing based An Efficient Lightweight authentication protocol for Smart Grid communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: A smart grid is a smart electrical power grid system that have smart meter, service provider, control centre and cloud centre. The smart grid gives number of advantage over power grid like data security, improved reliability, computerized data monitoring and an effective power consumption system. However smart grid have these advantages, but also the smart grid also faces certain security challenges that require attention. One of the key problems is that the data provided by smart metres is constantly changing and cannot handle excessive delay in an SG. There is also a security issue between the cloud centre and smart meter, which should be addressed. Edge computing, an extension of cloud computing, is a solution to these challenges and it can be implemented between a smart meter and a cloud centre. Paper presented, the proposed protocol is a lightweight authentication protocol that is based upon edge computing that can be used in an SG to address security challenges and ensure reliable communication between the cloud centre and the smart meters.

articleTitle: Online Shows Recommendations using Machine Learning in Big Data Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The use of machine learning has grown into a potent tool to handle enormous quantities of information in present-day information-driven surroundings. We are currently concentrating on developing systems based on artificial intelligence capable of suggesting videos on the internet for viewers of websites that stream content. We have uncovered essential components of these websites from our research, including movie information and user tastes, that could be used utilized to determine audience tastes while offering appropriate content that corresponds therewith these. In recent years, systems of recommendations have increased in favor of an approach. These types of systems provide choices for viewers for seeing movies they like according to a review of their behaviors and interests. Combining Big Data, Machine Learning, and engines for the recommendation, this research proposes an innovative approach to suggesting movies. We used an innovative approach termed Matric Factorising (MF), which may benefit form data mining techniques including segmentation and reducing dimensionality. This was applied to the Recruits-recommendation of the engine itself. Television series have moved into an entirely novel phase because of digital streaming platforms like Netflix as well as Amazon Prime. Company vast databases allow them to arrive at accurate projections regarding what information is going to be common, increasing their bottom lines and helping users to identify possibly fascinating fresh programming. In our study, algorithms for learning were implemented in an extensive data environment to analyze the popularity and achievement of different platforms. We observed that for forecasting the rating rates for programs in addition to additional variables like the style and given, classifiers based on random forests fared exceptionally well. The research presented here emphasizes just how important it is for utilizing algorithmic learning in big data events for one to learn about online entertainment and pick which shows to take in!

articleTitle: Deep Learning Recurrent Attention Optical Character Recognition Network with Data Augmentation for Cheque Data Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Bank cheques are often used for monetary transactions in many different fields. Before a check is cashed, it undergoes rigorous scrutiny. The normal verification process includes checking the date, signature, legal information, and cheque amount. This research uses a recurrent attention optical character recognition network (RA_OCRN) to extract legal information from a taken picture of a check in order to address these problems. In this work, we have utilized the recommended deep learning model to do data pretreatment and data augmentation, and we have compared the results to those obtained by using the already available methods. We run the model on the Kaggle cheque detection dataset, and we find that data augmentation improves the algorithm's detection accuracy. Results from the research show that RA_OCRN with data augmentation has the highest recognition accuracy and so has the greatest performance".

Author Keywords: recurrent attention optical character recognition network

articleTitle: Severity Grading of Diabetic Retinopathy Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR), an eye condition that affects patients with diabetes, actually destroys the retina and, over time therefore compromises the vision. Due to the complex grading system and the requirement for trained ophthalmologists to identify and evaluate numerous small characteristics that may indicate the presence and severity of the disease, diagnosing diabetic retinopathy (DR) using color fundus images is a difficult and time-consuming process. The grading system for DR is complex and includes several stages, each with specific features and severity levels that require careful evaluation. Additionally, identifying these features in retinal images can be difficult due to the small size of the structures, which may be easily overlooked or misinterpreted by the untrained eye. This can lead to misdiagnosis and delayed treatment, potentially resulting in irreversible vision loss. In order to sort high-resolution fundus pictures and automatically detect diabetic retinopathy, a Deep Learning based algorithm is suggested in this paper. In this paper, we show how to apply Diabetic Retinopathy convolutional neural network advanced (DR-CNN+) approach on colour fundus pictures to perform diabetic retinopathy grading detection and to classify retinal pictures into no DR, mild, moderate, severe, or proliferative DR, a dataset is trained. The dataset that was used in the training of algorithm consisted of 8,000 colored retinal pictures from the training set and 1600 photos from the testing set. The simulation results are shown to support the suggested strategy. As compared to the methods currently in use, it has been shown that the DR-CNN+-based algorithm that was proposed may attain a level of accuracy of 96%, sensitivity of 94.6%, and specificity of 91.24%.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Recurrent Neural Networks-LSTM and GRU for Automatic Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The work presented in this paper evaluates and compares the performance of the conventional Recurrent neural network(RNN), with elegant variations in the RNN architecture namely the LSTM and Gated Recurrent Units(GRU) for speech recognition. The conventional RNNs inept handling of the long-term dependencies due to the vanishing/exploding gradient problem led to the LSTMs and GRUs which specialises in handling long-term dependencies and does well in speech recognition tasks. The LSTM and GRU networks provide much greater frame precision than the RNNs while converging much more quickly. Further in the paper, the Unidirectional LSTMs and GRUs are extended to their bidirectional counterparts, which train input data in both the forward and reverse directions. The work presented in this paper clearly indicates a superior performance of the bidirectional models compared to their unidirectional counterparts. The bidirectional LSTM shows an accuracy of about 90% with a nominal loss of 0.0388 for the same training iterations and learning rate and being tested on a well established english speech commands data-set.

articleTitle: Analysis of Conventional PWM Techniques for Enhanced Ultra High Gain Z-Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: In these modern times, the Z-Source Inverters (ZSIs) has become a revolutionary invention ever since from the year 2002. The pulse-width modulation (PWM) technique used for most of the ZSIs is simple boost control PWM (SBC-PWM), the SBC-PWM implies for a greater voltage stress on the inverter bridge and provides less boost factor. Likewise, many topologies for the basic Z-source topologies are evolved and different PWM techniques are applied to them like maximum boost control (MBC), maximum boost control with third harmonic injection (MBC-THI), maximum constant boost control (MCBC), and constant boost control with third harmonic injection (CBC-THI). All these mentioned PWM techniques are compared and the converter opted in this paper is an Enhanced Ultra-High Gain active switched quasi-Z-Source Inverter [EUHG-qZSI]. The comparisons discussed in this brief are bridge stress, voltage gain and voltage boost variation under each control strategy implementation. The theoretical and simulation evaluation for the above findings is presented in this paper and the best PWM among them is Maximum Boost Control (MBC).

Author Keywords: CBC-THI and Enhanced Ultra-High Gain active switched quasi-Z-Source Inverter [EUHG-qZSI]

articleTitle: SFC-ACO: A Robust Path Failure Handling Method for Service Function Chaining in Kubernetes on OpenStack Magnum
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The increasing demand for scalable, flexible, and adaptable network infrastructures has led to the growing popularity of Network Function Virtualization (NFV) in modern networks. Virtual Network Functions (VNFs) and Cloud-Native Network Functions (CNFs) are virtualized network services that can be arranged in a specific sequence called Service Function Chaining (SFC). However, multiple path failures in the service function path pose a significant challenge for SFC. To address this issue, this research proposes an Improved Ant Colony Optimization (SFC-ACO) algorithm that integrates Mixed Integer Programming (MILP) constraints into the traditional Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm. The algorithm is implemented using Kubernetes Cluster with OpenStack Magnum. The proposed algorithm generates a path that meets CNF requirements while minimizing end-to-end delay and providing alternative paths in case of path failure. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in optimizing end-to-end delay compared to the generic ACO algorithm, highlighting its potential as a practical solution for network operators in 5G networks.

articleTitle: A New Proposed Data Security Model in Cloud Computing Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Advancement in the environment of cloud computing has rapidly increases over the past years. In cloud computing protection of data utilizing centralized resources has arisen because of a growing number of businesses storing their data int the cloud helps them easily to access their data easily. The major issues faced by users nowadays, the safety and fetching of user cloud data is arisen rapidly. In this proposed algorithm, the user's data is encrypted using the advanced encryption standards algorithm, and the encrypted data is then performed with some xor operations in cypher block chaining mode using a secret key known only to the data owner to increase confidentiality and security level. If the user does not provide a secret key, the system can generate one on its own.

articleTitle: Movie Recommendation System and Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: We are living in a digital era, nowadays everything starting from shopping to entertainment is easily accessible online to all the age groups, thanks to the user-friendly interface. This technological advancement was maximized during COVID-19 and continues to flourish till now. But this development made about 29.1 percent of the population that consists of children under the age of 18 vulnerable to movies, shows having illegal and adult content. Not only this, even for adults it can be a tiresome process to scroll through a long list of movies on sites just to find that one movie of your taste. In such cases, a recommendation system will help the user filter out the content easily. In this paper, we have done detailed data analysis over the IMDB movie dataset and created a recommendation system where users can look for movies on the basis of actor, director, genre, language etc. This system works using the concept of correlation and feature engineering.

articleTitle: An improved melting point detector algorithm for the determination of the melting point of crystalline chemical substances
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: The Automatic Digital Melting Point Apparatus is a key instrument in the pharmaceutical industry for determining the melting point of crystalline chemical substances. Our previous melting point detector algorithm employed change detection methods but had room for improvement. It relied on single pixel intensity values at specific locations in the chemical-filled capillary tube, which could produce inaccurate results if air bubbles were present. To address this issue, we developed an Improved Melting Point Detector (IMPD) algorithm that computes the intensity values of multiple pixels instead of just one. The IMPD algorithm solves the air bubble problem and provides more accurate results. We tested the IMPD algorithm on five crystalline chemical substances and achieved a maximum accuracy of 99.10% for magnesium nitrate and D-glucose.

articleTitle: Model Free Reinforcement Learning based Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Computer, Electronics & Electrical Engineering & their Applications (IC2E3)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drive plays a vital role in multiple applications, however, controlling of PMSM is a very complex task due to the presence of multiple nonlinear motor parameters which are directly dependent on its speed and current control mechanism. Traditional control algorithms such as vector control are badly impacted by these parameter variations. This research work presents the improved control topology under hybrid deep-reinforcement learning, which is more robust to changes in the motor parameters and loading conditions. Presented algorithm explicitly does not require the explicit plant model for tuning its parameters. Two control topologies based on the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm and deep Q network (DQN) are proposed for controlling the PMSM. Additionally, the objective function based on the weighted sum of error of the tracking d-axis and q-axis current is proposed for learning control topology parameters. Numerous experimental investigations on the proposed current control of a drive have been carried out to demonstrate its effectiveness. The result shows that the DDPG is more reliable and has higher d-axis and q-axis current tracking accuracy as compared to the deep Q-learning algorithm.

articleTitle: Empowering Last-Mile Connections: A Comprehensive Study on Emerging Technological Advancements
